sourcesDialog.ordersOfMagnitudeForTheHis: Orders of magnitude for the historical city, then the municipality, rather than the metropolitan area. Between documented anchors, the counter interpolates values and rounds them to the nearest thousand. Early estimates are uncertain and boundaries vary. The Antiquity anchor is about 20,000 inhabitants; early medieval variations are not reconstructed. After 2023, the latest census is retained.
sourcesDialog.theCompassSwitchesBetweenN: The compass switches between north and the visible map's reading orientation: 53° for 1777 or 84° for 1631. On the timeline, the incoming map becomes the reference halfway through the transition. Other maps face north. These approximate angles help with reading legends; distortions in old maps may remain.
sourcesDialog.onAComputerHoldTheSpaceBar: On a computer, hold the space bar to show the current map. Hold the eye button to read today's streets with a faint historical overlay. Release it to return to the previous view. Places takes you to a neighbourhood. Share creates a link to the current view, including your selected epochs and settings.
sourcesDialog.theTimelineBlendsTheMapsSe: The timeline blends the maps selected in Epochs with the current map. The tools above let you choose overlay, curtain or magnifier without changing the date. Available sources include Late Antiquity, twelfth- and thirteenth-century reconstructions, the 1550 parcel analysis, the 1631 and 1777 plans, the 1680 and 1830 cadastres, the 1848 État-major map, the 1860 and 1904 plans, the 1875 flood map and the 1954 aerial photograph. Intermediate positions are visual transitions, rather than reconstructions of those years.
sourcesDialog.openfreemapVectorMapBasedO: OpenFreeMap vector map based on OpenStreetMap. Update dates vary by feature; this is not a snapshot of the city on a specific date.
sourcesDialog.differencesMayReflectChang: Differences may reflect changes in the city or inaccuracies in historical documents. For the 1680 and 1830 cadastres, accuracy and control points are not published with the tiles. Alignment of every building is not guaranteed. Historical data is absent outside its coverage.
sourcesDialog.theOfficialCatalogueListsT: The official catalogue lists the Open Licence v2.0 for cadastral data. Terms specific to the rendering and hosting of Makina Corpus tiles remain to be confirmed. This version is for personal exploration of the concept; public distribution would require clarifying those terms or producing a layer from the open data.
details.blackAndWhiteAerialPhotographSup: Black-and-white aerial photograph supplied by IGN / Edugéo, already georeferenced. At high zoom, the photograph's pixels become visible. Outside its coverage, the current map remains displayed.
details.thePlanCoversTheCentreAndSuburbs: The plan covers the centre and suburbs, including Minimes, Bonnefoy, Saint-Cyprien and Saint-Michel. The Amidonniers bridge appears as a proposal. Grid numbers, title and margins are preserved.
details.planDeLaVilleDeToulouseDrawingBy: Plan de la ville de Toulouse. Drawing by Léon Laffont, lithograph by Pierre Rouy, published by Pagès et Carrère. Archives municipales de Toulouse, 20Fi57. 1904 print.
details.thePlanWasManuallyAlignedOn15Lan: The plan was manually aligned on 15 landmarks. At three independent control points, discrepancies are 14–27 m. Accuracy decreases at the edges. This historical document does not describe current flood risk.
details.originalSirvenLaDepechePlanArchi: Original Sirven / La Dépêche plan, Archives municipales de Toulouse, 20 Fi 45. Scan available on Mapas Milhaud. Blue indicates flooded areas; red indicates collapsed houses.
details.thePlanShowsTheRailwaySquaresAnd: The plan shows the railway, squares and suburbs. It includes completed changes and officially proposed alignments, distinguished by the legend. Inset maps and views of monuments are preserved.
details.villeDeToulouseFaubourgsBanlieue: Ville de Toulouse. Faubourgs. Banlieue. Drawing by Justin Jourdan, lithograph by Prosper Rivière. Archives municipales de Toulouse, 20 Fi 66 · public domain.
details.ignGeoreferencingRefinedOnRetain: IGN georeferencing refined on {{v0}} retained landmarks: junctions, bridges, monuments and axes around Grand Rond. {{v1}} independent checks verify this progressive realignment in the centre. Tiles cover zoom levels 6–15; beyond that they are enlarged. IGN source, Open Licence 2.0; metadata verified on 1 October 2026.
details.1848IsTheManuscriptDateInTheCata: 1848 is the manuscript date in the catalogue. Later additions, particularly railways, may appear in this series: not every depicted feature necessarily represents its 1848 state. The map mainly shows land, roads, crops and villages around the city; it does not provide parcel-level cadastral accuracy.
details.colourManuscriptSheetsAt140000Di: Colour manuscript sheets at 1:40,000, distributed by IGN. The official catalogue dates sheet 230 NO covering central Toulouse to 1848, as well as the five neighbouring sheets intersecting our navigation area. The period 1820–1866 refers to the national series rather than the date for Toulouse.
details.viewTheCompletePlanAndLegend: View the complete plan and legend
details.theCompletePlanPreservesItsTable: The complete plan preserves its tables and legend. Manual affine alignment on Saint-Sernin, Saint-Étienne and the right bank of Pont Neuf. Two separate checks show discrepancies of {{v0}} m. These landmarks do not guarantee accuracy elsewhere; street correspondence remains approximate, particularly at the edges.
details.planDeLaVilleDeToulouseDedieEtPr: Plan de la ville de Toulouse dédié et présenté à Monsieur le frère du Roi. Drawing by Joseph Marie de Saget, engraving by Pierre Gabriel Berthault. Archives municipales de Toulouse, II 686 · public domain. Original scan of 5906 × 4047 pixels.
details.theCompleteSheetPreservesItsMarg: The complete sheet preserves its margins, cartouche and legend.
details.revisedAlignmentOn22GroundLandma: Revised alignment on 22 ground landmarks, with a local correction at rue Nazareth. Four separate checks around Nazareth and Salin show discrepancies of 8–39 m, without establishing accuracy across the city. Monuments are drawn in perspective; roofs and edges remain less reliable. This plan does not guarantee exact street-by-street correspondence.
details.planDeLaVilleDeTholoseArchivesMu: Plan de la ville de Tholose, Archives municipales de Toulouse, II 671. Original scan of 7874 × 5884 pixels, public domain.
details.1550DatesTheReconstructedCadastr: 1550 dates the reconstructed cadastre used for analysis. Streets and buildings in the background particularly represent the 12th and 13th centuries: this is not a complete state of Toulouse in 1550. Alignment uses three churches; the independent check at Saint-Pierre-des-Cuisines shows a discrepancy of about {{v0}} m, without guaranteeing accuracy elsewhere.
details.compositeOfFigures7And8FromQuitt: Composite of figures 7 and 8 from Quitterie Cazes's study, drawn by F. Callède / Inrap. Red boundaries of ancient orientation in figure 7 supplement the blue boundaries in figure 8. The background and legend of figure 8 are preserved; figure 7's archaeological background remains in the original.
details.viewTheCompleteDrawingAndLegend: View the complete drawing and legend
details.affineAlignmentOnSaintSerninSain: Affine alignment on Saint-Sernin, Saint-Étienne and la Dalbade. An independent check at Saint-Pierre-des-Cuisines shows a discrepancy of about {{v0}} m, without guaranteeing accuracy elsewhere. The original legend is preserved on the map. The 1250 anchor in links and the timeline provides ordering; the source dates the plan to the 13th century without a precise year.
details.drawingByFCalledeInrapPcrToulous: Drawing by F. Callède, Inrap, PCR « Toulouse au Moyen Âge », illustration 6 from Quitterie Cazes's study published in Marquer la ville (2013), on OpenEdition. Known and proposed positions are distinguished in the original legend. Parcel boundaries aid reading rather than providing an exact 13th-century survey.
details.saintPierreDesCuisinesFigure3Sup: Saint-Pierre-des-Cuisines: figure 3 supplements the borough with red phases around 1100 and 1150 and the light green phase around 1180. The yellow 1050 phase, late medieval teal phase and later grey features are excluded. Phases are shown together for analysis without asserting that all walls coexisted. Two nave corners not used for alignment show discrepancies of {{v0}} m against IGN. These local checks do not guarantee accuracy elsewhere.
details.narbonnaisCastleApproximatePlace: Narbonnais castle: approximate placement based on the castle symbol in the general plan, north and the scale of figure 11. This fragment has no independent surveying check. The uncertain gate and possible entrances remain marked; the cadastral background does not represent a medieval state. Complete legends are accessible below.
details.saintEtienneOnlyRedRomanesqueFea: Saint-Étienne: only red Romanesque features, yellow canons' houses and the purple episcopal palace are retained in identified areas. The pale yellow 13th-century extension and later grey features are excluded. Two checks at corners of the current cathedral show {{v0}} m; they do not validate the entire district.
details.affineAlignmentTransferredFromTh: Affine alignment transferred from the 13th-century reconstruction, then corrected at the Saint-Sernin crossing on the current IGN map. The Saint-Pierre-des-Cuisines check against IGN shows {{v0}} m; the Porterie and Matabiau gates show {{v1}} m of disagreement with the 13th-century drawing. These checks do not guarantee historical accuracy or the alignment of every street. The complete drawing and legend are preserved.
details.threeSeparateAreasTheSaintSernin: Three separate areas: the Saint-Sernin borough, Romanesque features of the Saint-Étienne district and the late 12th-century Narbonnais castle. Undocumented areas between these fragments remain transparent. Saint-Sernin parcel boundaries analyse the reconstructed 1550 cadastre. The 1195 anchor provides ordering without precisely dating every feature.
details.partialReconstructionFigure9From: Partial reconstruction: figure 9 from Quitterie Cazes's study, drawn by F. Callède / Inrap. The document shows borough growth around 1107, around 1150, after 1150 and expansion after 1191. Colours and the legend distinguish these phases; this is not a single state of the entire city.
details.toulouseInThe12thCenturyThreeRec: Toulouse in the 12th century · three reconstructed areas
details.theSourceIndicatesLateAntiquityW: The source indicates Late Antiquity without a precise year. The 450 anchor in links and on the timeline is used only for ordering. The original legend is preserved. Affine alignment uses three reference churches; the independent check at Saint-Pierre-des-Cuisines shows a discrepancy of about {{v0}} m, without guaranteeing accuracy elsewhere.
details.figure1FromQuitterieCazesSStudyD: Figure 1 from Quitterie Cazes's study, drawn by F. Callède. The plan distinguishes remains of the Early and Late Roman Empire and proposed reconstructions of ancient street axes. Parcel boundaries and churches provide landmarks; the depicted elements are not all contemporary.
details.alignmentUsesLandmarksAcrossTheC: Alignment uses {{v0}} landmarks across the centre, canal bridges, Saint-Cyprien and Grand Rond, including the central basin and three street axes around the park, with progressive correction of the plan's distortions. {{v1}} independent checks at junctions, churches and squares show discrepancies of {{v2}} m. These checks concern the centre; they do not guarantee accuracy in the suburbs or at document edges. The complete sheet is preserved.
details.mapProducedByMakinaCorpusFromTou: Map produced by Makina Corpus from Toulouse Métropole's historical cadastre. This is a modern drawing of historical data, rather than an archive scan. Georeferenced tiles are used without additional distortion.
